text: The University of the Andes (Colombia) was founded in 1949 by Mario Laserna Pinzón, aiming to provide technically skilled professionals and leaders for Colombia’s development. It began with 80 students and a small set of faculties, modeled after American universities, and emphasized both technical and liberal education. The university maintained political neutrality and included government representatives in its board, ensuring good relations with conservative and liberal administrations. It established international exchange programs with over 119 universities in 34 countries and has a student body of 55% male and 45% female, with 95% of undergraduates being top 1% high school students. The campus, located in Bogotá, spans 180,551 sq m and includes 116 classrooms, 219 laboratories, a central library, and five satellite libraries with over 445,000 books. The university’s mascot is a goat named Seneca, symbolizing its founding era. Notable alumni include César Gaviria (President of Colombia), María Ángela Holguín (Ministry of Foreign Affairs), and Fernando Botero Zea (Ministry of National Defense). The university's mission emphasizes academic excellence, pluralism, diversity, and civic responsibility.
